problems.title: The problems VitNode solves for community sites.
problems.description: Six common headaches of running a community site, and what VitNode does about each one.

two_systems.problem: My blog and my forum run on two systems with two logins.
two_systems.answer: On VitNode, articles and forum topics live in one app with one member account. Roles, search, notifications and moderation work the same everywhere, so a reader who comments on an article can join the forum without signing up twice.

moderation.problem: Moderation is spread across plugins, bots and spreadsheets.
moderation.answer: Reports land on one ModCP board, where moderators claim them, leave notes and close them. Each forum section has its own approval rules, and a moderator can be limited to the sections they actually look after.

languages.problem: My readers speak more than one language.
languages.answer: Every field can hold a translation, every language gets its own URL, and hreflang tags and the sitemap are written for you. AI drafts the translation and flags the ones that fell out of date.

fees.problem: Licence fees grow with the community.
fees.answer: VitNode is MIT-licensed and free, with no paid tier and no member limits. You pay only for the server, and the code is yours to change. For comparison, Invision Community’s self-hosted licence costs $499 plus $199 a year.

plumbing.problem: Every new idea means rebuilding sign-in, roles and an admin panel.
plumbing.answer: Those parts ship in the core. A plugin adds only the feature: one content type definition gives you a database table, a typed API, AdminCP screens, revisions and search, in TypeScript from end to end.

not_developer.problem: I have the idea, but I’m not a developer.
not_developer.answer: Daily work happens in the AdminCP and ModCP, with no code. For setup and new plugins, hand the job to an AI coding agent: every docs page has a Markdown version, and the whole set is one file at /llms-full.txt.

what.question: What is VitNode?
what.answer: VitNode is a free, open-source community platform written in TypeScript. It gives a website members, roles, sign-in, an AdminCP, a ModCP, search, notifications and AI, and plugins add the forum, the blog or features of your own.

free.question: Is VitNode free?
free.answer: Yes. VitNode is MIT-licensed, with no paid tier and no member limits. You pay only for hosting, on your own server or a platform such as Vercel.

forum_blog.question: Can I run a forum and a blog on one site?
forum_blog.answer: Yes. The forum and blog plugins share one member account, one set of roles and one search, so articles and discussions sit side by side on the same domain.

self_hosted.question: Is VitNode self-hosted?
self_hosted.answer: Yes. It runs on Node.js with PostgreSQL, on a VPS, your own server or Vercel. Your members and content stay in a database you control.

developer.question: Do I need to be a developer to use VitNode?
developer.answer: Not for daily work, which happens in the AdminCP and ModCP. Installing the app and adding plugins happen in a terminal, and an AI coding agent can do those steps with the agent-ready docs.

production.question: Is VitNode ready for production?
production.answer: Not yet. VitNode 2.0 is a canary build, so expect bugs and breaking changes between releases. Today it suits new projects and prototypes.

different.question: How is VitNode different from Discourse or XenForo?
different.answer: VitNode treats articles and forum topics as content on one TypeScript core, with per-field translations and AI budgets built in. Discourse and XenForo are mature forum products with more discussion features today. The comparison pages go through it row by row.
